recipes.name: Creamed Eggs on Toast
ingredients_raw: salt and white pepper to taste

steps.text: Separate egg whites from egg yolks. Place egg yolks into a bowl and mash with a fork. Chop egg whites into small pieces and set aside.

Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat; stir in flour until smooth. Gradually mix in milk and chicken bouillon so that no lumps form and stir constantly until mixture comes to a boil. Add mashed egg yolks and mix until dissolved. Stir in chopped egg whites.
Serve over toast and season with salt and white pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Creamed Eggs on Toast
raw_recipe.description: Creamed eggs on toast made with an easy white sauce is a delicious and comforting way to use leftover hard-boiled eggs for breakfast or brunch.

review.reviewBody: I have been making (and eating) Creamed Egg for years. I never thought I'd see a recipe in print - I thought it was something my Mother made up! She made lots of vatiations, using browned hamburger, or browned sausage, or creamed dried beef instead of the hard boiled eggs. The basic sauce recipe is so versitile that you could creme anything! I bet some crumbled bacon would be delicious with the eggs in this recipe. This recipe is a little different from my Mother's in that it called for Chicken Boullion. I gave it a shot and got great reviews. I made it for breakfast yesterday for my two best friends and they loved it! They wanted the recipe. I directed them to allrecipes.com! Thanks for another great recipe (one I thought my Mom was the only one who knew how to make it)

I have never ever tried this & this looks really yummy. In my scrambled eggs I found a secret & I hope you try this I add 1 teaspoon per egg Sour Cream whisk very well until very well incorporated no white should be seen. It makes them so creamy,fluffy & delicious do this before scrambling them. I also add some Garlic Powder,Onion Powder/Dried Chives,Salt & Pepper to taste. A few dabs of butter then scramble I place my skillet on high heat & whisk until done their done in 1 minute. Or I lightly butter spray a left over stouffers small size lasagna container I save these & reuse them then sprinkle all around the container salt this helps them rise like a souffle. Microwave 30 seconds stir then again 30 seconds in intervals until done. All microwaves vary.

I have made a version of this for years. Easiest way is to make a roux. Butter and flour 1-1. Use milk or half and half. 
Also we add velveeta cheese and let it melt. 
We serve it over toasted English muffins. 
One other thing - just cut up the eggs. - Don’t separate them and don’t mash the yolks
Yummy!

This is one of my mother's comfort foods. I have been making it for nearly 50 years. There are so many variations to be made. As other posters have mentioned, dried beef is a good addition. Actually, any kind of leftover meat would be good. In order to get some veggies in, some times I will add frozen green peas (which also adds a nice pop of colour). For those who find it too bland, I would suggest adding some Worcestershire sauce or experimenting with some of your favourite herbs or spices. There are lots of possibilities for "perking it up".

I will still make my old family recipe, making a wine cream sauce, with dry mustard, garlic powder, mixed herb spice and only the chopped hardboiled whites in the cream sauce, with the whole yolks grated over the creamed egg white mixture after you have used the sauce mixture to cover the toast. When you mix in the yolks, it is not as appetizing looking...like a dog's breakfast, as Ina Garten says...

wasn't sure about it but this was excellent. made it for one, but there is enough left over for tomorrow morning. a little rich but good. i made a roux, did not separate the whites from the yolks but just chopped them, added a pinch of tarragon, some chopped bacon and green onions. quite colourful. i would make this for company staying over.

This recipe is also known as Eggs a la Goldenrod. It can be served attractively with a slight variation. As an alternative in preparing this, add only the chopped egg whites to the cream sauce. Cut the toasted bread into toast points, pour the sauce over them and garnish with the crumbled egg yolks. Sprinkle with paprika and serve immediately.

My mom made this and I consider it comfort food. A nice warm on the tummy breakfast (although once made I eat it 24/7 till gone hahaha). Last time I made I tossed in a bit of parmesan cheese so it was like a light cheese sauce. I never ever use the green shaker bottle of parmesan, or what I call fake parm. I think real grated parmesan taste better and has better texture, green can can be gritty at times. Even better to buy a chunk of parmesan and grate fresh to use. My mom served on toast but honestly it's so much better on a fluffy biscuits. The sauce is so light yet rich it suits a biscuit better in my opinion. I have added finely shaved ham, bacon, sprinkled on finely diced green onions, etc. The variation ideas are endless. I like to add a couple of drops if liquid smoke sometimes, when I do it reminds me of campfire breakfast.

I rated this 4 stars as it is missing on incredible important variation to the OP. My grandmother made this for me all the time and hers before her. The name of this dish is Golden Rod Egg. The trick is not to include the crumbled yolk to the egg mixture. You take the crumbled yolk and use it as a topping on the egg mixture after adding it to the toast. Think a crumble on top like green bean casserole except you don’t combine anything to the crumbled yolk. Top that with some green onion or scallion and granny would be proud.

I ran out of milk had to use .5 cup of water. still good will make again. I use chinese White pepper.very powerful stuff only sprinkle a little on top. I also enhanced bread. croisant bread from local chinese bakery 4 pieces of toast 3 tablespoons olive oil wash both sides of bread sprinkle of Parmesan cheese . grilled on medium heat both sides about 2 minutes each. My roomates loved it. Cut the recipe in have 6 eggs still a 3rd left over.

I did not make this, but my grandmother used to make something like this. she called it Goldenrod Toast. She would divide the whites and the yolks of the hard boiled eggs. the whites would be chopped up and added to the sauce. the crumbled yolks would be garnish on top. then add a sprinkle of paprika. It's quite pretty that way.
Loved it! I made 1/2 recipe with no changes except used 1 cup milk with 1/2 cup half and half. Also grated 2 bouillon cubes so they mixed in easily. Will definitely make this again.
Loved it!!
Loved the idea. Made mine low carb for one person. Cream cheese, butter, heavy cream melted together, stirred the mashed yolks in first, then added the cut whites. Happy to have found this recipe.

This was pretty tasty. I made a couple of changes - I realised after I had boiled the eggs that I was out of milk so just used chicken stock, and I served it on toasted seeded bread rather than white. I really liked whisking the mashed egg yolks into the sauce - made a great flavour.
This recipe is really good. I usually mash whole hard boiled eggs and add cream until smooth. Salt, pepper, and some crumbled bacon.

Lots of feedback they it’s bland. I’ve been making this since I was taught to as a child. How to make it less bland? what I add: some grated onion, dried parsley, paprika, dill, onion powder and a pinch of nutmeg. Also heat into the sauce some green peas (not a lot) or shelled edamame. I like it best on crescent rolls but also on Italian or sourdough toast or even on just white rice. Anytime you make a cream sauce either milk be sure to add enough salt and pepper. Milk tends to negate the salt.

Hubby and I both loved this! We had never even heard of this dish before, but I read about it in a book and decided we needed to try it. We have ducks and chickens and have an abundance of eggs so I’ll be adding this to my ‘I need to get rid of some eggs’ recipe file. I used a dozen duck eggs so it was extra eggy, rich, and delicious. I seasoned with salt, pepper, onion powder, turmeric, and a pinch of red pepper flakes.
Delicious, I usually only added milk, but I love the addition of chicken bouillon cubes, I used leftover chicken broth. Great flavor.

I was looking for something different to have for breakfast and tried his. I probably won't make it again as it was really bland. I didn't separate the yolks from the whites, not necessary. It all blended together well. Hubby thought it was good.
